title: Two Sum
description:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target.

You may assume each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

Input: line 1 is the array as JSON, line 2 is the target.
Output: the two indices as a JSON array, e.g. [0,1].

harness.python:
import sys, json
__lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
print(json.dumps(two_sum(json.loads(__lines[0]), int(__lines[1])), separators=(",", ":")))

title: Valid Parentheses
description:
Given a string s containing just the characters '()[]{}', determine if the input string is valid.

An input string is valid if open brackets are closed by the same type of bracket and in the correct order.

Output: 'true' or 'false'.

harness.python:
import sys
__lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
__s = __lines[0] if __lines else ""
print("true" if is_valid(__s) else "false")

title: Maximum Subarray
description:
Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) with the largest sum and return that sum.

Input: a single line containing the array as JSON, e.g. [-2,1,-3].
Output: the maximum subarray sum as a single integer.

examples.explanation: The subarray [4,-1,2,1] has the largest sum 6.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description:
Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring that contains no repeating characters.

Input: a single line containing the string s (it may be empty). The test strings contain no spaces.
Output: the length as a single integer.

examples.explanation: The answer is "wke". Note "pwke" is a subsequence, not a substring.

constraints: s consists of English letters, digits and symbols (no spaces in tests).

harness.python:
import sys
__lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
__s = __lines[0] if __lines else ""
print(length_of_longest_substring(__s))

title: House Robber
description:
You are a robber planning to rob houses along a street. Each house has some money, but adjacent houses have connected security systems that trigger if two adjacent houses are robbed on the same night.

Given an integer array nums representing the money in each house, return the maximum amount you can rob without alerting the police.

Input: a single line containing the array as JSON.
Output: the maximum amount as a single integer.

title: Coin Change
description:
You are given coins of different denominations and a total amount of money. Return the fewest number of coins needed to make up that amount. If it cannot be made from any combination of the coins, return -1. You have an unlimited number of each coin.

Input: line 1 is the coins array as JSON; line 2 is the target amount.
Output: the fewest number of coins (or -1) as a single integer.

harness.python:
import sys, json
__lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
print(coin_change(json.loads(__lines[0]), int(__lines[1])))

title: Trapping Rain Water
description:
Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.

Input: a single line containing the heights array as JSON.
Output: the total units of trapped water as a single integer.

examples.explanation: The elevation map traps 6 units of water.

title: Edit Distance
description:
Given two strings word1 and word2, return the minimum number of operations required to convert word1 into word2. The permitted operations are: insert a character, delete a character, or replace a character.

Input: line 1 is word1; line 2 is word2.
Output: the minimum number of operations as a single integer.

examples.explanation: horse -> rorse (replace h) -> rose (delete r) -> ros (delete e).

constraints: Both strings consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Contains Duplicate
description:
Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice, and false if every element is distinct.

Input: a single line containing the array as JSON.
Output: 'true' or 'false'.

harness.python:
import sys, json
__nums = json.loads(sys.stdin.read().splitlines()[0])
print("true" if contains_duplicate(__nums) else "false")

title: Valid Anagram
description:
Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, and false otherwise. An anagram uses all the original letters exactly once.

Input: line 1 is s; line 2 is t.
Output: 'true' or 'false'.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters.

harness.python:
import sys
__lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
print("true" if is_anagram(__lines[0], __lines[1]) else "false")

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description:
You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a stock on day i. You want to maximise profit by choosing a single day to buy and a later day to sell.

Return the maximum profit you can achieve. If no profit is possible, return 0.

Input: a single line containing the prices array as JSON.
Output: the maximum profit as a single integer.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 1 (price 1) and sell on day 4 (price 6): profit 5.
Prices only fall, so no profit is possible.

title: Climbing Stairs
description:
You are climbing a staircase that takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can climb either 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you reach the top?

Input: a single line containing the integer n.
Output: the number of distinct ways as a single integer.

title: Binary Search
description:
Given a sorted (ascending) array of distinct integers nums and a target, return the index of target if it is present, otherwise return -1. Your algorithm should run in O(log n) time.

Input: line 1 is the array as JSON; line 2 is the target.
Output: the index (or -1) as a single integer.
constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order and all values are distinct.

harness.python:
import sys, json
__lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
print(search(json.loads(__lines[0]), int(__lines[1])))

title: Majority Element
description:
Given an array nums of size n, return the majority element - the element that appears more than n/2 times (rounded down). You may assume the majority element always exists.

Input: a single line containing the array as JSON.
Output: the majority element as a single integer.
constraints: A majority element always exists in the array.

title: Single Number
description:
Given a non-empty array nums where every element appears exactly twice except for one, find that single element. Aim for linear time and constant extra space.

Input: a single line containing the array as JSON.
Output: the element that appears once, as a single integer.
constraints: Every element appears twice except for one which appears once.

title: Product of Array Except Self
description:
Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] equals the product of all elements of nums except nums[i]. Solve it without using the division operator.

Input: a single line containing the array as JSON.
Output: the answer array as a JSON array, e.g. [24,12,8,6].
constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix fits in a 32-bit integer.

title: Move Zeroes
description:
Given an integer array nums, move all 0s to the end while keeping the relative order of the non-zero elements. Return the resulting array.

Input: a single line containing the array as JSON.
Output: the resulting array as a JSON array.

title: Longest Common Prefix
description:
Write a function to find the longest common prefix string amongst an array of strings. If there is no common prefix, return an empty string.

Input: a single line containing the strings as a JSON array, e.g. ["flower","flow","flight"].
Output: the longest common prefix (an empty line if there is none).
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Roman to Integer

Input: a single line containing the Roman numeral.
Output: the integer value.
constraints: s is a valid Roman numeral in the range [1, 3999].

harness.python:
import sys
__lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
__s = __lines[0] if __lines else ""
print(roman_to_int(__s))

Input: a single line containing the integer n.
Output: the answer as a JSON array of strings.

title: Caesar Cipher
description:
Encrypt a message with a Caesar cipher: shift each lowercase letter forward in the alphabet by a given amount, wrapping from z back to a. The shift may be larger than 26.

Input: line 1 is the message (lowercase letters only); line 2 is the integer shift.
Output: the encrypted message.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Run-Length Encoding
description:
Compress a string by replacing each run of consecutive identical characters with the character followed by the run length. For example "aaabbc" becomes "a3b2c1". The empty string encodes to the empty string.

Input: a single line of text (lowercase letters, possibly empty).
Output: the run-length encoded string.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

harness.python:
import sys
__lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
__s = __lines[0] if __lines else ""
print(run_length_encode(__s))

title: Digital Root
description:
Repeatedly sum the digits of a non-negative integer until a single digit remains, and return that digit. For example 38 -> 3 + 8 = 11 -> 1 + 1 = 2.

Input: a single line containing the integer n.
Output: the digital root as a single integer.
